subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should OpenClaw treat configured cross-provider model fallback as consent to transfer user media, or add a separate provider media trust policy for fallback retries?
rationale: The source shows a real privacy boundary gap, but the permanent default affects compatibility, fallback usefulness, and sensitive-data disclosure, so automation cannot safely choose the security/product policy.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Add config, docs, and runtime checks that preserve existing behavior by default while letting users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

options.title: Document configured fallback as full consent
options.body: Keep current forwarding semantics and document that configured cross-provider fallbacks may receive prompt text, images, and attachment-derived image data.

options.title: Fail closed for cross-provider media
options.body: Strip cross-provider media by default and require users to opt back into forwarding when they want fallback vision behavior.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Add config, docs, and runtime checks that preserve existing behavior by default while letting users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the current fallback image replay behavior on main and is closest to the affected implementation path.
